reason: Conversation 1 reasons coherently from the customer's answers, explains the sump/pump/float chain, and gives a front-only glass-of-water test that works around the stacked unit. It stays honest about uncertainty, doesn't name a definite faulty part or part number, and says an engineer is the sensible next step if the pump looks at fault. Conversation 2 gives disjointed, template-like replies, asks irrelevant questions such as 'staying dry underneath' and about the blower fan at the back, which the customer can't reach, and ends with a generic engineer referral without explaining the likely pump/sump issue or suggesting any further front-only checks. Conversation 1 is a bit long and the glass-of-water test adds minor risk, but it is far more useful.
